cues.text: Symphony treats agent code as untrusted.
People run the CLI and the Tern plugin, with an API token.
cues.say: People run the C L I and the Tern plugin, with an API token.

cues.text: The edge is a Cloudflare Tunnel. It only dials out.
The trusted side runs the API, the daemon, the runners, the merger and Redis.
cues.say: The trusted side runs the API, the daemon, the runners, the merger and Red-iss.

cues.text: It keeps the integration credentials, and makes every write that needs them.
The agent runs in a workspace pod, which gets only the credentials of its own attempt.
Agents call model providers with API keys.
Host cloud credentials, such as Amazon Bedrock, and custom endpoints with no authentication also work.
Symphony has no provider OAuth and no subscription login.
cues.say: Symphony has no provider O auth and no subscription login.

cues.text: An admin stores a key from Tern or the CLI.
cues.say: An admin stores a key from Tern or the C L I.

cues.text: Keys are write-only. Tern shows only whether a key is set.

scenes.title: A closed network and no Kubernetes token

cues.text: Each attempt runs in its own workspace pod.
Its NetworkPolicy allows no ingress, and egress only to the gateway, DNS and public addresses.
cues.say: Its network policy allows no ingress, and egress only to the gateway, D N S and public addresses.

cues.text: Private ranges are excluded: no API, Redis, node or metadata endpoint.
cues.say: Private ranges are excluded: no API, Red-iss, node or metadata endpoint.

cues.text: The pod mounts no ServiceAccount token, so it cannot call the Kubernetes API.
cues.say: The pod mounts no service account token, so it cannot call the Kubernetes API.

cues.text: Nothing connects into the pod. The runner uses pods/exec.
cues.say: Nothing connects into the pod. The runner uses pods exec.

cues.text: Public egress is open, so agent code can leak only its own credentials.
A workspace gets four credentials.
The model credential of its role, and a GitHub token for the ticket's repositories.
The telemetry token of the dispatch, and one MCP token for each agent session.
cues.say: The telemetry token of the dispatch, and one M C P token for each agent session.

cues.text: The runner writes them into private files.
The pod never holds the Linear key, the App private key, chat tokens or API tokens.

scenes.title: A narrow scope that lasts one hour

cues.text: A normal ticket gets the GitHub scope ghapp.WORKSPACE.
cues.say: A normal ticket gets the GitHub scope G H app dot workspace.

cues.text: It writes code and pull requests, and reads checks, actions and statuses.
It has no issues, projects or workflows permission.
An investigation gets ghapp.READ_ONLY, so GitHub refuses its push or pull request.
cues.say: An investigation gets G H app dot read only, so GitHub refuses its push or pull request.

cues.text: A token lives at most one hour. The runner renews it between turns.

scenes.title: Secret headers stay in the gateway

cues.text: An admin picks MCP servers for each agent role.
cues.say: An admin picks M C P servers for each agent role.

cues.text: Their secret headers live in a Secret that only the gateway mounts.
The gateway drops the agent's Authorization and adds the stored headers.
Each agent session gets its own MCP token, for one role.
cues.say: Each agent session gets its own M C P token, for one role.

cues.text: Another role, or a disabled server, gets a 403.
cues.say: Another role, or a disabled server, gets a four oh three.

cues.text: The token is revoked when the session ends.
Symphony ignores repository MCP configs, and turns tools.xdev off.
cues.say: Symphony ignores repository M C P configs, and turns tools dot x dev off.

cues.text: Setup checks each integration credential with its service, then saves it in a Secret.
Only an admin can write them, and no response or log shows them.
Each identity has a namespaced Role. The API only patches Secrets that exist before setup.
cues.say: Each identity has a namespaced role. The API only patches Secrets that exist before setup.

cues.text: Webhooks need a valid HMAC signature, and they only wake a loop.
cues.say: Webhooks need a valid H MAC signature, and they only wake a loop.

cues.text: Fencing makes sure that only the current dispatch of a ticket can change state.
API tokens have three roles. A viewer reads.
An operator also acts: pause, hold, interrupt and bypass.
An admin also manages tokens, provider keys and setup.
The API stores only a SHA-256 hash of each secret.
cues.say: The API stores only a shaw two fifty-six hash of each secret.

cues.text: A token gets 600 requests a minute. Above a limit, the API answers 429.
cues.say: A token gets six hundred requests a minute. Above a limit, the API answers four twenty-nine.

cues.text: The API audits every command and every provider change.

scenes.title: Read-only agents, and a person confirms

cues.text: The assistant answers in Slack and Discord. Every message is untrusted.
Its agents can only read and search. They have no bash, edit or write.
They hold no chat, tracker or App credential, and read code with a read-only token.
An agent can propose tickets, but a proposal creates nothing.
Only a person mapped in notify.users can confirm.
cues.say: Only a person mapped in notify dot users can confirm.

cues.text: Local mode has no container. The agent runs as the host user.
Symphony strips its own secrets from the agent's environment. That is hygiene, not a boundary.
With a GitHub App, each attempt still gets a scoped token in a private file.
There is no NetworkPolicy, and your own MCP config still loads.
cues.say: There is no network policy, and your own M C P config still loads.

cues.text: Use a dedicated user, and run only tickets from people you trust with a shell.
